name: Gigbinder
idea: Offline-first web app for gigging bands: charts, setlists, transposition and band sync that does not break on every update.
description: Musicians keep PDF charts and ChordPro/lyric sheets in one place, build setlists, transpose with correct enharmonic spelling and capo hints, and run a full-screen stage mode that turns pages with a Bluetooth foot pedal (pedals send plain key presses, which browsers receive). Charts stay in the device (IndexedDB); only setlist order, keys and notes sync through Supabase so the whole band sees the same list. Hard to copy because of the chart-format importers (ChordPro, OnSong-style text, PDF), music-theory-correct transposition, and offline-first sync with conflict handling.
web_delivery: PWA on Vercel; PDFs and text charts cached in IndexedDB via service worker; Supabase stores only small setlist and band-membership rows.
why_hard_to_copy: Offline-first sync with conflict handling plus music-theory-correct transposition and several chart-format parsers; a CRUD setlist list is easy but a trustworthy stage tool is not.

name: Parenting Plan Calendar
idea: Free custody-schedule engine that turns a parenting-plan pattern plus holiday rules into one shared calendar and ICS feed.
description: Parents choose a base rotation (alternating weeks, 2-2-3, 5-2-2-5, custom) and then add holiday and school-break rules the way plans are actually written (even/odd years, first/second half of winter break, Friday-to-Monday weekends). The engine resolves rule precedence and outputs a color-coded year view, a printable PDF and a read-only ICS link for each parent's phone. Hard to copy because the value is the correctness of the rules engine and its holiday and school-calendar definitions, not the calendar UI.
web_delivery: Next.js on Vercel; rules engine is pure TypeScript run in the browser; the schedule is saved as one Supabase row and served as an ICS route handler.
why_hard_to_copy: Rule-precedence and holiday date algebra (odd/even years, split breaks, make-up days) is correctness-critical logic with many edge cases, plus a curated library of holiday and school-break definitions.

name: StitchTrack
idea: Browser-based tracker that reads a cross-stitch or knitting chart PDF and lets you tap off stitches and rows, offline.
description: Stitchers upload a born-digital pattern PDF; the app extracts the chart grid, symbols and thread legend in the browser, lets you mark completed stitches, highlight one thread colour, and count rows, saving progress locally and syncing to Supabase. It is aimed at people who buy PDF patterns from Etsy and pattern shops and are tired of subscription trackers and lost libraries. Hard to copy because reliable PDF chart parsing across pattern-maker layouts (symbol detection, legends, backstitch) is fiddly and needs a library of tested layouts.
web_delivery: PWA on Vercel; pdf.js parses the PDF in the browser; chart image and progress live in IndexedDB, only small progress rows sync via Supabase.
why_hard_to_copy: Client-side extraction of symbol grids and legends from PDFs produced by many different pattern tools, plus thread-brand (DMC/Anchor) mapping, which needs a tested corpus of real patterns.

name: LeagueSlate
idea: Ad-free team and league schedule hub with a constraint-based schedule generator and per-team calendar feeds.
description: League coordinators enter teams, fields, time slots, blackout dates and rest rules; the generator builds a balanced round-robin or pool-play schedule, and parents subscribe to their team's ICS feed with live field changes. No ads, no mandatory app, just a link and email/ICS updates. Hard to copy because the constraint scheduler (home/away balance, field limits, coach conflicts) and low-disruption rescheduling after rainouts are real algorithmic work.
web_delivery: Next.js on Vercel; scheduler runs in the browser; league data in Supabase; ICS per team via a route handler; Supabase Realtime for live field changes.
why_hard_to_copy: Constraint scheduling with fields, slots, blackouts and rest rules, and minimal-change rescheduling, is an optimization problem rather than CRUD; several free generators exist but none is combined with an ad-free team hub.

name: PubOpen
idea: Open and convert old Microsoft Publisher .pub files to PDF, SVG or editable text entirely in the browser.
description: Microsoft Publisher stopped being part of Microsoft 365 on 1 October 2026, so offices, schools and clubs are left with years of .pub newsletters, flyers and labels they can no longer edit. This tool parses the legacy .pub container in the browser (nothing is uploaded) and exports a PDF, page images and the extracted text and fonts for rebuilding in Word or Canva. Hard to copy because .pub is an obscure reverse-engineered binary format and good fidelity needs a WebAssembly build of an existing parser plus lots of real-world test files.
web_delivery: Static site on Vercel; the parser (libmspub compiled to WebAssembly) runs fully client-side, so there is no server cost and no file upload.
why_hard_to_copy: Parsing a proprietary legacy binary format client-side with decent layout fidelity; the work is porting a C++ library to WASM and tuning it against a corpus of real .pub files.

signals.summary: A university IT notice tells staff Microsoft 365 users can no longer open or edit .pub files after 1 October 2026 and advises converting to PDF or rebuilding in Word or PowerPoint; the page was updated again on 23 October 2026.

name: BracketForge
idea: Free, no-paywall tournament engine with Swiss, double-elimination and group-to-playoff formats and live spectator pages.
description: Organisers of community game nights, school clubs and local esports events create a bracket without hitting a paywall, using correct Swiss pairing with tiebreaks, double elimination with grand-final reset, seeding byes and multi-stage formats. Players join by link with no account and results update live on a spectator screen. Hard to copy because pairing and tiebreak rules are correctness-critical and the live-sync layer must be reliable at venue Wi-Fi quality.
web_delivery: Next.js on Vercel; pairing engine in TypeScript; results and live standings through Supabase Realtime; public read-only spectator URL.
why_hard_to_copy: Swiss pairing with Buchholz-style tiebreaks, bye handling, double-elimination reset logic and re-seeding after dropouts are rules-engine problems with many edge cases, and live results need dependable realtime sync.

name: TripPaste
idea: Paste or drop travel confirmations and get a clean itinerary with a calendar feed, without needing an email-sync service.
description: Travellers paste confirmation emails, upload .eml files or PDFs, and the app extracts flights, hotels, trains and car rentals using hand-built per-supplier parsers, then builds a day-by-day itinerary, time-zone-correct ICS feed and shareable page. It targets people frustrated that email auto-import in the big itinerary apps stopped working or duplicates calendar entries. Hard to copy because accurate extraction from many airline, hotel and rail confirmation formats is a maintained library of parsers and edge cases such as time zones and multi-leg trips.
web_delivery: Next.js on Vercel; parsing runs in the browser (pdf.js for PDFs, text rules for emails); itineraries stored in Supabase with a public share link and ICS route.
why_hard_to_copy: A growing, tested library of supplier-specific confirmation parsers with correct time-zone and multi-leg handling, which generic LLM-free code cannot guess.

name: SowRight
idea: Garden planner that gets planting dates right: local frost dates, crop-specific rules and succession planting, with no subscription.
description: Gardeners enter a location and bed layout; the planner uses frost-date normals and a hand-checked crop rules table (days to maturity, soil-temperature limits, direct sow vs transplant, succession intervals) to generate a dated sow, transplant and harvest calendar that updates as crops are harvested. It is for home vegetable growers who have caught consumer garden apps giving wrong advice or locking basics behind subscriptions. Hard to copy because the value is an expert-verified, region-aware crop dataset and scheduling logic, not the UI.
web_delivery: Next.js PWA on Vercel; crop rules and frost-date data are static JSON (public NOAA-style normals); user beds and plantings in Supabase.
why_hard_to_copy: A curated and verified crop-rules dataset by climate and frost date plus succession and harvest-date logic; generic AI-generated advice is the exact failure reviewers describe.

name: Lingua Reader
idea: Browser reader for language learners: click any word for a dictionary entry, track known words, no forced AI and no per-month wall.
description: Learners paste or import articles, EPUBs and subtitle files, and the app splits them into words (including Japanese, Chinese and Thai with browser-native segmentation), colours each word by how well you know it, and shows an offline dictionary entry on click. Known-word counts, lemma handling and an Anki-ready export are built in, and a text's vocabulary coverage is shown before you start reading. It targets people leaving LingQ-style paid readers over mandatory AI features and instability. Hard to copy because tokenisation, lemmatisation across inflections and the bundled open dictionaries (Wiktionary, JMdict, CC-CEDICT) are language-by-language data and NLP work.
web_delivery: Next.js PWA on Vercel; dictionaries and segmentation data shipped as per-language packs cached in IndexedDB; word-status rows synced through Supabase.
why_hard_to_copy: Per-language segmentation, lemmatisation and dictionary pipelines (CJK, Thai, inflected European languages) plus accurate known-word tracking across word forms; a flashcard clone is easy, this is not.

name: Field Checklist
idea: Offline-first birding checklist logger that never loses unsubmitted lists and exports eBird-ready CSV.
description: Birders log species counts, location, time and protocol in the field with no signal, using an offline taxonomy of species names and codes; lists stay on the device and sync when online, and a validated CSV in eBird's import layout is generated so nothing is retyped. Birders can start a list for any place, not just near their GPS fix, and edit past lists in bulk. Hard to copy because of the offline taxonomy handling, protocol and date/location validation rules that eBird's importer enforces, and loss-proof offline-first storage.
web_delivery: PWA on Vercel with a service worker and IndexedDB; taxonomy as a static JSON pack; optional Supabase sync; CSV generated in the browser for eBird's web import tool.
why_hard_to_copy: Offline-first storage that cannot lose lists, plus a maintained taxonomy and importer-validation rule set; the eBird CSV format has strict requirements (one date, one location, a protocol per list).

name: AAC Board Hub
idea: Free web AAC board editor with backup, sharing and ready-made therapist-built page sets so a family never loses years of setup.
description: Parents and speech therapists build symbol-and-word boards for non-speaking children or adults, speak them with the browser's built-in speech, and keep them backed up in the cloud so a broken tablet does not wipe years of customisation. Boards can be shared as links or copied from a library of page sets that follow common core-word layouts. Hard to copy because the value is the board import/export plumbing and vetted vocabulary page sets, not the grid UI.
web_delivery: PWA on Vercel using the Web Speech API for voice and IndexedDB for offline boards; board JSON and shared links in Supabase; symbols limited to openly licensed sets.
why_hard_to_copy: Importing and exporting boards between AAC systems and curating vetted core-vocabulary page sets takes speech-language-pathology knowledge; the UI alone is a weekend project.

name: Course Rescue
idea: Import a Canvas/Common Cartridge or QTI export and turn it into a free, hosted mini-course with auto-graded quizzes.
description: Independent teachers, tutors and homeschool co-ops lost free tools in 2026: Canvas Free-for-Teacher shut down after a final export window in July, Padlet retired its teaching tools, and GitHub Classroom closed. This app imports a .imscc or QTI export in the browser, rebuilds modules, pages and quizzes, and hosts them with a student login-free code link, auto-grading and CSV grade export. Hard to copy because Common Cartridge and QTI exports vary by tool version and quiz question types (numeric tolerance, matching, multi-answer) must be graded correctly.
web_delivery: Next.js on Vercel; the export is parsed client-side with a zip library; course JSON in Supabase; grading in Supabase Edge Functions; media kept as links to limit storage.
why_hard_to_copy: Parsing .imscc and QTI variants and reproducing Canvas quiz-question scoring semantics is format-specific, correctness-critical work.
